doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

chapter: Richmond and arriving in New York
title: Tunes you must know at a session
summary: Rhythm changes, Cherokee, blues; the Giant Steps and It's You or No One stories and Harold Mabern's advice.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Off the top of your head, what are let’s say five tunes that you better know inside and out if you’re going to get up on a jam session?
Well there’s standard rhythm changes, of course in B flat but be ready to do them in any key. “Cherokee,” the blues, that never changes, and of course you could always throw in

a couple of American Songbook standards, you know, “Green Dolphin Street,” “All the Things You Are.” But basically those three, those first three. And of course well you could throw “Giant Steps” in there because eventually somebody’s going to throw that at you.

Yeah. One of the tunes, actually one of the tunes that I had never really learned when I first moved to New York and it got called on me a couple of times was — what’s the title of it — [scats]. I can’t think of the title of it now unfortunately [scats].
I guess I don’t know it either.

Yeah I’m getting bad with titles. But I went home and learned that off a Dexter Gordon record because someone called it on me at a jam session one night and I thought okay. And I remember Harold Mabern telling me some years later, when he was in Chicago cutting his teeth and it happened to him all the time. And he says, “Yeah well you know first time shame on you, second time shame on me.” So he said yeah, whenever that happens go home and learn that tune immediately. Oh, “It’s You or No One.”
So yeah, I learned from that experience.
Like you can never know all of them it seems like.
